title: Unified Subagent Orchestration Platform Plan (Full Spec v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Umbrella architecture and operating model for OpenClaw subagent orchestration. Execution is now sequenced through three deliverable slice plans: orchestrator core lite, linear+scheduler integration, and recurring jobs framework.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Provide a single generalized orchestration system that can reliably execute ad-hoc task batches, long-running queues, and recurring operational jobs with deterministic state, observable artifacts, and safe integrations.

sections.heading: Problem Statement
sections.body: Current ad-hoc subagent orchestration suffers from completion signaling gaps, inconsistent Linear transitions, fragmented retry behavior, and occasional session lookup/pairing failures that block execution. This produces status drift and operational overhead.

sections.heading: Scope (In)
sections.body:
• Subagent lifecycle orchestration
• Task scheduling + dependency handling
• Linear update safety model
• Recurring job pipeline framework
• Run artifacts, metrics, and operator reporting
• Failure handling for session/pairing/API disruptions

sections.heading: Scope (Out, v1)
sections.body:
• Fully autonomous product strategy decisions
• Cross-org multi-tenant scheduling
• Complex priority optimization engines
• Deep anti-cheat/security enforcement beyond current operational needs

sections.heading: Design Principles
sections.body:
1) Deterministic orchestration state over conversational memory.
2) Evidence-gated completion, never trust plain-text success claims.
3) Centralized mutator model for external state systems (Linear).
4) Idempotent operations first; retries should be safe by default.
5) Fail-soft for recurring jobs: partial data still yields useful output.
6) Clear operator visibility with concise but complete status artifacts.

sections.heading: Reference Architecture
sections.body:
A) Orchestrator Core (runtime scripts + state store)
B) Orchestrator Skill (agent contract, prompts, guardrails)
C) Worker Sessions (spawned subagents, bounded task scope)
D) Integrations (Linear, Discord reporting, repo artifacts)
E) Scheduler Modes (one-shot, queue, recurring cron)

sections.heading: State Machine (Run-Level)
sections.body:
Run states: `queued -> preparing -> running -> blocked -> recovering -> done|failed|canceled`.
Rules:
• `queued -> preparing`: inputs validated, lock acquired.
• `preparing -> running`: at least one eligible task dispatched.
• `running -> blocked`: frontier empty due to blockers/dependency/policy conflict.
• `blocked -> recovering`: recovery action or retry window starts.
• `recovering -> running`: recovery clears blocker.
• Terminal states: `done` (all required tasks complete with evidence), `failed` (unrecoverable policy/runtime error), `canceled` (operator/user stop).

sections.heading: State Machine (Task-Level)
sections.body:
Task states: `ready -> claimed -> executing -> validating -> done|blocked|failed|canceled`.
`done` requires validator pass + evidence schema complete.
`failed` indicates retry budget exhausted or hard policy violation.
`blocked` requires reason code + next action hint.

sections.heading: Worker Input Contract (Required)
sections.body: Each worker receives structured JSON input: `run_id`, `task_id`, `objective`, `acceptance_criteria[]`, `allowed_paths[]`, `disallowed_actions[]`, `linear_issue_id`, `reporting_channel`, `timeout_s`, `retry_index`, `dependency_context`, `policy_refs[]`.

sections.heading: Worker Output Contract (Required)
sections.body: Each worker must emit structured result JSON: `run_id`, `task_id`, `session_key`, `outcome` (`done|blocked|failed`), `summary`, `evidence` (commit hashes, file paths, test/check outputs), `linear_proposal` (requested transition/comment), `blocker` (reason code + remediation), `timestamps` (start/end). Free-form completion text is non-authoritative.

sections.heading: Evidence Validation Gates
sections.body:
A task cannot transition to `done` unless all gates pass:
1) Required evidence fields present
2) Acceptance criteria mapped to evidence entries
3) Repo/check commands (if specified) pass
4) Any required artifact files exist
5) Proposed Linear transition is policy-valid for current issue state.

sections.heading: Linear Mutation Safety Model
sections.body: Centralize all Linear writes in orchestrator-core mutator. Workers only propose transitions. Mutator enforces: read-fresh-before-write, idempotency keys, allowed transition matrix, policy references, and race detection (issue changed since read). On race, re-read and re-evaluate before mutating.

sections.heading: Dependency Scheduling (DAG Frontier)
sections.body: Scheduler computes in-degree from dependency relations. Eligible set = tasks with unresolved blocker count = 0 and status `ready`. Queue mode draws from frontier only. Completion of a task decrements dependent in-degree and may unlock new frontier nodes.

sections.heading: Execution Modes
sections.body:
• Sequential: max active workers = 1 (default safety mode).
• Windowed: max active workers = N (bounded, explicit).
• Queue Worker: long-running runner polls eligible frontier repeatedly with sleep interval and lock checks.
All modes use same contracts/state machine.

sections.heading: Failure Taxonomy + Reason Codes
sections.body:
Standard reason codes: `session_lookup_unavailable`, `pairing_required`, `api_timeout`, `policy_violation`, `dependency_blocked`, `validation_failed`, `repo_conflict`, `unknown_runtime_error`.
All non-done outcomes require reason code.

sections.heading: Recovery + Retry Policy
sections.body:
• Retry classes: transient vs persistent.
• Transient (lookup timeout/API): bounded exponential backoff with jitter.
• Persistent (policy violation/missing required input): no blind retry, escalate immediately.
• Per-task retry budget default: 2 attempts after initial run.
• Per-run circuit-breaker: fail run if failure ratio exceeds threshold or repeated identical failures occur.

sections.heading: Session/Pairing Disruption Handling
sections.body: If session lookup/pairing blocks dispatch, move task to `blocked` with reason `pairing_required` or `session_lookup_unavailable`, emit operator alert, and queue for retry window. Preserve claim metadata to avoid orphaned ownership. Never silently drop task context.

sections.heading: Recurring Pipeline Framework
sections.body:
Implement recurring jobs as staged pipelines:
1) Capture stage(s): collect scoped source signals into normalized artifacts
2) Merge stage: combine artifacts, resolve conflicts, compute summary objects
3) Publish stage: post formatted output once per schedule
Each stage has deterministic input/output schema and independent retries.

sections.heading: Morning Standup Reference Pipeline (Example)
sections.body:
A) Source capture jobs (janitor, bug scanner, Linear digest)
B) Merge job composes final standup object
C) Publisher posts to standup channel once
Behavior on missing source: degrade gracefully with explicit unavailable note, do not skip standup post.

sections.heading: Artifact and Storage Contract
sections.body: Store run artifacts under a dedicated orchestration path with per-run folder: metadata, task events, worker outputs, validation results, final summary. Include immutable run id and timestamps. Artifacts are source of truth for audits and postmortems.

sections.heading: Observability + Metrics
sections.body:
Track at minimum:
• Run success rate
• Task success/block/fail counts
• Mean time to done
• Retry counts by reason code
• Linear mutation conflict rate
• Recurring pipeline completion rate
Publish concise ops summary each run and maintain machine-readable logs.

sections.heading: Operational Reporting Contract
sections.body: For each run, post lifecycle updates (started / completed / blocked / failed) to configured ops channel. Completion summary includes run id, completed tasks, blocked tasks with reason codes, key evidence links, and recommended next actions.

sections.heading: Security + Guardrails
sections.body:
• Restrict worker file write scope to approved repo paths per task.
• Require explicit approval for destructive operations.
• Do not auto-close issues without evidence gates.
• Reject ambiguous policy states; escalate instead.
• Keep secrets out of worker output artifacts.

sections.heading: Implementation Plan (Phased)
sections.body:
Phase 1 — Contracts + state machine + artifact schema
Phase 2 — Core runtime scripts (`start-run`, `dispatch`, `validate`, `close-run`)
Phase 3 — Linear mutator integration + dependency scheduler
Phase 4 — Recurring pipeline toolkit + standup reference implementation
Phase 5 — Hardening: failure injection tests, alert thresholds, operator runbooks

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• 100% of done tasks include valid evidence payloads
• Linear status drift incidents approach zero under orchestrated runs
• Session/pairing disruptions create recoverable blocked states, not orphaned work
• Recurring pipelines produce deterministic artifacts and single publish events
• Operators can reconstruct any run from artifacts without chat history dependence

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
• Risk: Contract overhead slows small tasks. Mitigation: lightweight sequential mode presets.
• Risk: Validator false negatives. Mitigation: narrow invariant checks + versioned validator updates.
• Risk: Reporting noise. Mitigation: concise summaries + channel scoping.
• Risk: Integration drift with Linear. Mitigation: centralized mutator + freshness checks.

sections.heading: Task Breakdown Guidance (for Linear conversion)
sections.body:
Create one epic plus dependency-linked tasks:
1) Spec + contracts
2) Core runtime scripts
3) Validator + evidence gating
4) Linear mutator
5) DAG scheduler
6) Recurring pipeline primitives
7) Standup reference pipeline
8) Observability + alerting
9) Hardening + docs

sections.heading: Next Step
sections.body: Execute implementation via the three slice plans in sequence (A then B then C), while using this umbrella plan for architecture guardrails and contract consistency checks.

sections.heading: Execution Sequencing Update
sections.body:
This unified plan is retained as an umbrella/reference spec and is superseded for implementation sequencing by:
1) `subagent-orchestrator-core-lite-v1` (Slice A)
2) `subagent-linear-scheduler-integration-v1` (Slice B)
3) `subagent-recurring-jobs-framework-v1` (Slice C)
Delivery order: Slice A -> Slice B -> Slice C. Cross-slice changes must preserve worker input/output contracts and evidence gating invariants defined here.

title: Slice A — Orchestrator Core Lite (Deliverable Spec v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Implement the minimum production-safe orchestrator core: deterministic run/task state machines, worker contracts, artifact persistence, and evidence-gated completion without external mutator integrations.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Deliver a reliable core orchestration runtime that can execute bounded task runs end-to-end with deterministic state, structured worker I/O contracts, and auditable artifacts.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: In: run/task state models, dispatch loop (sequential + bounded window), worker contract envelopes, artifact schema, evidence validation gates, lifecycle reporting, recovery for transient runtime failures. Out: Linear writes, advanced dependency graph scheduling beyond simple ready frontier, recurring cron pipelines.

sections.heading: Architecture/Design
sections.body: Components: (1) Run Coordinator (lock, initialize, lifecycle transitions), (2) Task Dispatcher (claim/launch/reclaim), (3) Validator (contract + evidence gate checks), (4) Artifact Store writer, (5) Reporter. Canonical states: run `queued->preparing->running->blocked|done|failed|canceled`; task `ready->claimed->executing->validating->done|blocked|failed|canceled`. All transitions are append-only evented with timestamps and actor metadata.

sections.heading: Contracts
sections.body: Worker input required fields: `run_id`, `task_id`, `objective`, `acceptance_criteria[]`, `allowed_paths[]`, `disallowed_actions[]`, `reporting_channel`, `timeout_s`, `retry_index`, `dependency_context`, `policy_refs[]`. Worker output required fields: `run_id`, `task_id`, `session_key`, `outcome`, `summary`, `evidence`, `blocker`, `timestamps`. Validation contract: `done` only when required fields are present, acceptance criteria mapping is complete, and required artifacts/check outputs are attached.

sections.heading: Implementation Phases
sections.body:
Phase A1: Define JSON schemas for run, task, worker-input, worker-output, and validation result artifacts.
Phase A2: Build `start-run` + dispatch executor for sequential mode with lock handling.
Phase A3: Add bounded windowed mode and retry policy (transient-only exponential backoff + jitter).
Phase A4: Implement validator and run finalizer (`close-run`) with evidence-gated task completion.
Phase A5: Add operator reporting templates and basic failure-injection tests.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• A run with 5 tasks executes deterministically and produces complete per-run artifacts without relying on chat memory.
• 100% of tasks marked `done` pass schema and evidence gate checks.
• Session/pairing lookup interruptions produce explicit `blocked` or retriable failures with reason codes, never silent drops.
• Restarting coordinator during `running` recovers from persisted artifacts and does not duplicate completed task closure.
• Lifecycle updates post started/completed/blocked/failed summaries to configured channel.

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
Risk: Contract strictness slows early adoption. Mitigation: ship schema examples + helper generators.
Risk: State corruption from concurrent coordinators. Mitigation: repo/process lock + run ownership token.
Risk: Validator false failures. Mitigation: versioned checks with explicit invariant list and test fixtures.
Risk: Operator alert noise. Mitigation: concise aggregation and reason-code bucketing.

sections.heading: Next Step
sections.body: Create Linear epic and tasks for A1-A5, then implement Phase A1 and A2 first with contract fixture tests before enabling multi-task runs.

title: Slice B — Linear + Scheduler Integration (Deliverable Spec v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Add centralized Linear mutation safety and dependency-aware scheduling on top of the core orchestrator so external issue state and internal task execution remain consistent under concurrency.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Integrate policy-safe Linear updates and DAG frontier scheduling into the orchestrator to eliminate state drift between execution artifacts and issue tracker status.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: In: centralized mutator, read-fresh-before-write enforcement, transition policy checks, idempotency keys, race detection/reconcile loop, dependency graph frontier scheduler, blocked reason taxonomy alignment. Out: recurring pipeline framework and cron stage orchestration (Slice C).

sections.heading: Architecture/Design
sections.body: Add two subsystems: (1) Linear Mutator Service invoked only by coordinator after task validation; workers submit `linear_proposal` only. (2) Dependency Scheduler maintaining adjacency + in-degree indexes per run and dispatching only eligible frontier nodes. Conflict path: mutator detects stale issue revision -> re-read -> re-evaluate transition -> apply or downgrade to `blocked(policy_violation|race_conflict)`.

sections.heading: Contracts
sections.body: Task definition contract extends with `dependencies[]` and optional `linear_issue_id`. Worker output includes `linear_proposal` object (`target_state`, `comment`, `policy_refs`, `idempotency_key`). Mutator response contract: `applied|noop|rejected|conflict` plus evidence payload (pre/post state, timestamps, policy check results). Scheduler contract guarantees only dependency-satisfied tasks are claimable.

sections.heading: Implementation Phases
sections.body:
Phase B1: Implement dependency parser + DAG frontier calculator with cycle detection.
Phase B2: Wire scheduler into dispatch loop and unblock dependents on validated completion.
Phase B3: Implement Linear mutator adapter with freshness checks and allowed transition matrix.
Phase B4: Add race/conflict reconciliation flow and idempotent retry behavior.
Phase B5: Add integration tests for drift prevention (simulated concurrent updates) and scheduler correctness.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• Scheduler never dispatches a task whose dependencies are incomplete.
• Cyclic dependency plans are rejected at preparation with actionable diagnostics.
• Workers cannot directly mutate Linear; all writes route through mutator with audit evidence.
• Concurrent Linear changes are detected and reconciled without invalid transitions.
• For orchestrated runs, issue-state drift incidents are reduced to near-zero in test and pilot usage.

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
Risk: Transition policy ambiguity. Mitigation: explicit matrix + per-project config and fail-closed defaults.
Risk: API rate limits. Mitigation: batched reads, bounded retries, and no-op detection via idempotency keys.
Risk: Complex DAG debug burden. Mitigation: export frontier snapshots and human-readable dependency diagnostics.
Risk: Mutator single-point failure. Mitigation: retry queue with durable pending intents and operator escalation.

sections.heading: Next Step
sections.body: After Slice A is stable, create Linear tasks for B1-B5 and start with B1/B3 in parallel test branches, then integrate through end-to-end drift tests.

title: Slice C — Recurring Jobs Framework (Deliverable Spec v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Build a staged recurring-job framework (capture, merge, publish) that reuses orchestrator contracts/artifacts to run reliable scheduled operational pipelines such as morning standups.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Provide deterministic, observable recurring pipelines that execute on schedule, degrade gracefully on partial source failure, and publish exactly one consolidated result per run.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: In: recurring run registration, stage model (`capture->merge->publish`), per-stage schema contracts, schedule trigger integration, partial-failure handling, final publish guardrails, runbook/ops metrics. Out: broad multi-tenant scheduler platform and non-operational content workflows.

sections.heading: Architecture/Design
sections.body: Recurring framework sits on top of slices A/B. Scheduler trigger creates run envelopes tagged `recurring`. Stages execute as orchestrated tasks with deterministic artifact paths: `captures/*`, `merge/summary.json`, `publish/result.json`. Publish stage is protected by single-fire guard (`run_id + stage_id` idempotency). Missing capture artifacts are represented explicitly in merge output with `unavailable` reason metadata.

sections.heading: Contracts
sections.body: Pipeline definition contract: `pipeline_id`, `schedule`, `sources[]`, `merge_strategy`, `publish_target`, `retry_policy`, `timeouts`. Stage output contracts: Capture -> normalized source artifact + freshness metadata; Merge -> combined summary object + source health map; Publish -> delivery receipt (channel/message ids) + rendered payload hash. Framework contract requires one and only one terminal publish attempt outcome (`done|blocked|failed`) per scheduled run.

sections.heading: Implementation Phases
sections.body:
Phase C1: Define pipeline manifest schema and recurring run bootstrapper.
Phase C2: Implement capture stage toolkit and source adapters with independent retries.
Phase C3: Implement merge engine with conflict rules and unavailable-source annotations.
Phase C4: Implement publish stage with exactly-once idempotency guard and fallback reporting.
Phase C5: Deliver morning standup reference pipeline + dashboards/runbook for operators.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• Scheduled runs create consistent run artifacts for every stage.
• If one or more capture sources fail, merge still produces output with explicit unavailable annotations.
• Publish stage emits at most one successful post per run and records receipts/hashes.
• Operators can replay/debug any recurring run from artifacts alone.
• Morning standup reference pipeline posts reliably during pilot window with actionable partial-failure messaging when needed.

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
Risk: Schedule overlap causing duplicate runs. Mitigation: per-pipeline run lock and overlap policy (`skip|queue`).
Risk: Source instability. Mitigation: stage-local retries + stale-data fallback with freshness flags.
Risk: Publish duplication on retries. Mitigation: idempotency key and receipt reconciliation before send.
Risk: Pipeline sprawl. Mitigation: manifest review checklist and shared stage libraries.

sections.heading: Next Step
sections.body: After Slice B validation, create Linear tasks for C1-C5 and implement C1/C2 first, then ship the standup reference pipeline as the pilot recurring workload.

title: Game Generator Determinism Plan (Hybrid Scaffold + Deferred Smoke)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Prioritize experiment traceability first: version and track game-generation skill prompts and stamp each generated game with its exact skill prompt version, then implement deterministic pipeline hardening with a hybrid scaffold and deferred smoke checks.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Increase predictability and reliability of game generation and publishing without reducing gameplay creativity. Lock brittle plumbing, keep mechanics/theme open-ended, and make verification resilient to GitHub Pages build latency.

sections.heading: Priority Shift (Do First)
sections.body: Before any reliability/scaffold work, implement experiment traceability for skill evolution. The top priority is to version game-generation prompt/skill changes and record, for every generated game, which exact skill prompt version produced it. This is required for valid comparison of skill improvements over time.

sections.heading: Design Principles
sections.body:
1) Experiment traceability is mandatory: every generated game must be attributable to an exact skill prompt version.
2) Deterministic where fragility is high (deploy, manifest, required wiring).
3) Flexible where creativity matters (mechanics, art direction, progression flavor).
4) Validators enforce contracts, not aesthetics.
5) Deployment success and Pages availability are separate phases.

sections.heading: Phase 1 — Deterministic Pipeline Foundations
sections.body:
Implement core scripts:
• `scripts/preflight-gamehub.mjs`: environment + credential + repo access checks.
• `scripts/lib/manifest.mjs` + `scripts/validate-manifest.mjs`: canonical games.json schema validation/upsert/formatting.
• `scripts/publish-game.mjs`: single deploy path (lock, copy, manifest upsert, commit, push retry/rebase).
All generation flows must publish through this CLI, not ad-hoc shell snippets.

sections.heading: Phase 2 — Hybrid Scaffold (Reliability Rails, Creative Core)
sections.body:
Introduce `templates/phaser-hybrid-base.html` with strict/open boundaries:
• Locked: constants, leaderboard helpers, menu wiring, game-over form/submit/replay flow, hub link plumbing.
• Open: gameplay systems, hazard/pickup behavior, scoring flavor (within required monotonic contract), theme/art/audio implementation.
Use explicit insertion regions so agents can fully vary game design while reusing stable plumbing.

sections.heading: Phase 3 — Contract Validation (Not Style Policing)
sections.body:
Add `scripts/validate-game-html.mjs` that checks required invariants only:
• Hub backlink present
• No `prompt()` for player-name submission
• Required leaderboard constants/functions present
• Keyboard + touch/pointer input hooks present
• Expected scene lifecycle anchors present (menu/start/game-over/replay path)
Do not enforce palette, genre, mechanics, or presentation style.

sections.heading: Phase 4 — Prompt Normalization With Creative Headroom
sections.body: Add `scripts/compile-game-spec.mjs` to normalize user prompt into a minimal structured spec (controls, loop/death, hazards, pickups, scoring contract, difficulty intent, visual/audio intent). Treat this as invariant guidance and completeness scaffolding, not a strict blueprint.

sections.heading: Phase 5 — Two-Stage Verification for GitHub Pages Latency
sections.body:
Use split verification:
• Immediate blocking checks (must pass before reporting deploy success): preflight, manifest/game validation, git push success.
• Deferred non-blocking check: `scripts/smoke-pages-url.mjs` starts after a delay (e.g. +2 minutes) and retries with backoff for a bounded window (e.g. up to 15 minutes). Report pass/fail asynchronously after Pages settles.

sections.heading: Operational Reporting Model
sections.body: Initial publish response returns: commit hash, slug, URL, and "Pages verification pending" state. Deferred smoke emits follow-up status with HTTP/content marker results and optional leaderboard-read check outcome.

sections.heading: Execution Order
sections.body:
0) Skill prompt versioning + per-game provenance stamping (required first)
1) Preflight + manifest + publish CLI
2) Game HTML contract validator
3) Hybrid scaffold template
4) Prompt/spec normalizer
5) Deferred smoke verifier
6) Orchestrator wrapper and metrics reporting

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• 100% of newly generated games include required skill prompt provenance fields (`skill_prompt_version`, `skill_prompt_commit`).
• Historical games are either backfilled with provenance or explicitly marked unknown (no silent nulls).
• Zero deploys performed via ad-hoc deploy scripts once migration completes.
• Zero new games missing required hub link or leaderboard plumbing contracts.
• No immediate false-negative deploy failures caused by GitHub Pages propagation delay.
• Gameplay/theme variance remains high (validators do not reject on creative differences).
• Pipeline produces machine-readable artifacts for task tracking and postmortems.

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
• Risk: missing/inaccurate provenance invalidates experiment conclusions. Mitigation: make provenance fields required in publish path and block release when absent.
• Risk: scaffold over-constrains style. Mitigation: lock only brittle plumbing and keep gameplay/theme blocks fully open.
• Risk: deferred checks get ignored. Mitigation: make deferred result post mandatory follow-up status.
• Risk: validator drift with evolving game conventions. Mitigation: keep validator focused on stable interface contracts and version it with template updates.

sections.heading: Next Step
sections.body: Convert phases into Linear tasks with explicit dependencies and ownership, then implement Phase 1 first as highest reliability ROI.

sections.heading: Skill Prompt Versioning System (Phase 0 — Required First)
sections.body:
Implement immutable prompt version tracking for the game generation skill:
• Add a canonical `skillPromptVersion` identifier (e.g., semver or date+hash) for each meaningful skill/prompt revision.
• Store version metadata in-repo (changelog + mapping to commit hash).
• Require each generation run to resolve and emit the active prompt version from source-of-truth files, not manual entry.
• Treat prompt version changes as first-class experimental events with audit trail.

sections.heading: Per-Game Provenance Stamping (Phase 0 — Required First)
sections.body:
Extend game metadata contract so every game record includes generation provenance fields:
• `skill_prompt_version` (required)
• `skill_prompt_commit` (required, commit hash that contained prompt/skill logic)
• optional `generation_run_id` / `generator_pipeline_version` for deeper debugging
Update `games.json` validation + upsert scripts to hard-fail if required provenance fields are missing for new games.

sections.heading: Historical Backfill + Unknown Handling
sections.body: For existing games, backfill provenance where confidently reconstructable from git history/records. For unresolvable cases, set explicit sentinel values (e.g., `skill_prompt_version: "unknown"`) plus notes, never silent omission. Analysis queries must distinguish known vs unknown provenance.

sections.heading: Experiment Reporting Requirements
sections.body: All experiment comparisons and quality summaries must segment by `skill_prompt_version`. Any cross-version aggregate must disclose version mix and sample sizes. No claim of improvement should be made without provenance-complete slices.

title: Batch Sequencer Skill (General Subagent Orchestration) - Draft
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: General-purpose skill spec for executing user-requested batches of Linear tasks via subagents with sequential/windowed modes, guardrails, retries, and evidence-based completion.

sections.heading: Disposition (2026-02-24)
sections.body: Status: RETIRED / SUPERSEDED. Superseded by `unified-subagent-orchestration-platform-v1` as the unified orchestration model. Keep for historical reference only; do not execute as active plan unless explicitly re-approved.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Create a reusable skill that can run a user-specified set of tasks as a controlled batch, using subagents while preventing concurrency drift and state desync.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.body: Required: project/repo path, task set (explicit IDs or range), execution mode (`sequential` or `windowed`), max concurrency, acceptance checklist, and reporting channel. Optional: allowed labels/lane filter, retry policy, blocked timeout, model overrides.

sections.heading: Execution Modes
sections.body:
Sequential mode (default): exactly one task active at a time.
Windowed mode: up to N active tasks, where N is explicit and bounded.
Both modes must enforce issue-lock checks before spawn.

sections.heading: Core Workflow
sections.body:
1) Resolve candidate tasks from input set.
2) Validate each task is eligible (state + required labels + ownership lane).
3) For each selected task: spawn one subagent (`sessions_spawn`) with bounded instructions.
4) Wait for completion signal; collect evidence (commit/hash/check output).
5) Update Linear notes/state only if acceptance criteria pass.
6) Continue until batch complete or blocked threshold reached.

sections.heading: Guardrails (Required)
sections.body:
• Never start a task already in-progress by another worker.
• In sequential mode, if any batch issue is in-progress, do not start another.
• Require commit/check evidence before Done.
• Enforce required label schema before pickup (`source:*`, `lane:*`, `kind:*`, `exec:*`, `agent:*` as applicable).
• If ambiguous state/conflict, escalate instead of mutating.
• Scheduler must compute dependency in-degree from Linear relations and only start nodes with in-degree=0.

sections.heading: Retry + Escalation Policy
sections.body: Per-task retry budget (default 1-2 repair attempts). On failure after retries: set Blocked/comment blocker reason and continue or halt based on user mode. Escalate hard blockers to designated channel with actionable next step.

sections.heading: Output Contract
sections.body:
Each run produces:
1) machine-readable run artifact (`batch-run-report.json`)
2) concise channel summary (started/completed/blocked)
3) Linear evidence updates per touched issue.
Summary includes task IDs, outcomes, commit links, and unresolved blockers.

sections.heading: Minimal v1 Deliverables
sections.body:
1) Skill spec + trigger guidance.
2) Standardized orchestrator prompt template.
3) Reusable subagent task prompt template.
4) Example command patterns for sequential and windowed batches.
5) Checklist for safe adoption in new projects.

sections.heading: Open Decisions
sections.body:
1) Default halt behavior on first blocker (halt vs continue).
2) Whether windowed mode is allowed by default or opt-in only.
3) Whether reporting channel is per-run input or fixed project config.
4) Whether parent epic auto-close is enabled by default.

sections.heading: Dependency Scheduling Rule (DAG)
sections.body: Task selection must use dependency graph in-degree: only pick tasks with unresolved blocker count (in-degree) = 0. Use Linear `blocked by` relations as graph edges. Tasks with in-degree > 0 are blocked and cannot be started. In windowed mode, schedule from the in-degree=0 frontier only.

title: Janitor Sync Architecture (Cron-First + Heartbeat Assist)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Define a durable anti-drift janitor system where cron scripts are source-of-truth for reconciliation and heartbeat remains optional triage commentary.

sections.heading: Disposition (2026-02-24)
sections.body: Status: RETIRED / SUPERSEDED. Superseded by `unified-subagent-orchestration-platform-v1` as the unified orchestration model. Keep for historical reference only; do not execute as active plan unless explicitly re-approved.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Eliminate status/plan/routing drift across Linear, repo planning docs, and agent execution by introducing a deterministic janitor-sync loop.

sections.heading: Operating Model
sections.body: Primary: cron-driven script(s) with strict checks and safe auto-fixes. Secondary: heartbeat prompt for summarization, prioritization, and escalation text only. Heartbeat is not source of truth.

sections.heading: Scope of Checks (v1)
sections.body:
1) Linear parent/child status consistency
2) Linear done-vs-backlog mismatch against recent delivery evidence
3) Required label schema validation (`source:*`, `lane:*`, `kind:*`, `exec:*`, `agent:*` where applicable)
4) `data/planning/plans.json` implementationStatus/taskTrackerStatus reconciliation
5) Stale In Progress issues timeout checks with blocker tagging

sections.heading: Auto-fix Policy
sections.body: Auto-fix only low-risk deterministic cases: close parent when all children done, add missing required labels from inferred lane/project defaults, update plan status fields from Linear majority signal. Any ambiguous case opens/updates a drift report issue instead of mutating state.

sections.heading: Cadence
sections.body: Run janitor cron every 30–60 minutes. Generate one concise drift report artifact each run: no-op (clean) or actionable mismatches grouped by severity.

sections.heading: Observability
sections.body: Persist run logs to repo-local state (`memory/heartbeat-state.json` or dedicated janitor log), include: run id, checks run, fixes applied, unresolved alerts, and links to affected Linear issues.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• Zero parent/child mismatch older than 24h
• Zero completed implementation left in Backlog for >24h
• Plan status fields never stale beyond one janitor interval
• 100% of new operational issues contain required labels

sections.heading: Task Breakdown
sections.body: Implementation tasks are tracked in Linear under Long-Term Planning / GAM-7 epic.

sections.heading: Reporting Channel Constraint
sections.body: All janitor user-facing summaries and escalation reports must post only to Discord channel `1475309759300239380`. No fallback to triggering/current channel. Full machine logs remain local/artifacted; channel output should be concise operational summaries.

title: Game Ratings Rollout Plan (Supabase + Existing Games)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Implement production game ratings across existing GameHub games using current Supabase stack: one rating per user per game (latest wins), 1-5 scale, aggregate display in game pages and hub cards, with staged rollout and validation.

sections.heading: Research Findings
sections.body: Current state: Supabase migration is live with `game_ratings` table, rating RPCs (`upsert_game_rating`, `get_game_rating_summary`), and shared client utility (`shared/supabase-client.js`) exposing rating helpers. Existing games are already wired to shared Supabase scripts for leaderboard compatibility but most game UIs do not yet expose a rating interaction flow. This means backend capability exists; missing layer is UI integration + aggregate surfacing + QA pass.

sections.heading: Requirements (confirmed)
sections.body:
• Rating scale: integer 1-5
• Identity model: anonymous client fingerprint, one rating per game per user, latest rating wins
• Keep GitHub Pages static architecture
• Use Supabase direct client path (no Worker dependency)
• Use existing games first (retrofit), then apply to new games by default

sections.heading: Architecture Approach
sections.body: Use `window.GameHubSupabase.upsertRating(gameSlug, rating)` and `window.GameHubSupabase.getRatingSummary(gameSlug)` from `shared/supabase-client.js`. Add a small reusable rating widget snippet to game pages (post-game overlay and/or persistent corner UI). Store/refresh aggregate summary in-page after submit. Extend hub rendering to show per-game average + count sourced from Supabase RPC (batched where practical).

sections.heading: Implementation Plan (phased)
sections.body:
Phase 1 — Shared UI primitives
1) Add reusable rating widget helper script under `shared/` for stars/buttons, loading state, submit state, and summary rendering.
2) Define consistent UX copy and edge-case behavior (no rating yet, submit failed, retry).

Phase 2 — Existing game integration
3) Patch active game pages to include rating widget and call Supabase rating APIs.
4) Ensure game slug binding is correct per page.
5) Ensure latest-rating overwrite behavior is reflected in UI (replace previous vote).

Phase 3 — Hub surfacing
6) Update `index.html` cards to display `avg_rating` and `rating_count`.
7) Optionally add sortable filter: Top Rated / Most Rated.

Phase 4 — Validation + hardening
8) Add smoke checklist script: submit rating, change rating, verify aggregate updates.
9) Verify no secret exposure in client artifacts.
10) Validate RLS behavior for anonymous writes and reads.

Phase 5 — Operationalization
11) Add default requirement to generation templates: include rating widget hooks.
12) Track adoption metric: % active games with working rating UI.

sections.heading: QA / Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
A rollout is complete when:
• A user can rate any active game 1-5
• Re-rating the same game updates (not duplicates) that user’s latest value
• Aggregate avg/count updates and is visible both in game UI and hub cards
• Failure states are non-blocking and user-visible
• No `secretKey` appears in shipped frontend files

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
• Legacy/non-shared game pages in active set (e.g., inline Supabase clients) can break one-size-fits-all widget rollout -> add compatibility mode in shared widget + force pilot coverage on at least one legacy page before scale rollout.
• Ambiguous active scope can cause partial retrofit -> define rollout scope explicitly as games.json entries with `archived !== true`, and require an inventory checklist before GAM-43 completion.
• Hub aggregate fetch fanout can degrade load UX if done per-card -> require batched summary path (or enforced request budget) in GAM-44 before done.
• QA evidence drift (manual-only verification) can let regressions slip -> require reproducible smoke command/checklist artifact in GAM-45 completion evidence.
• Generation template contract can drift from real integration behavior -> gate GAM-46 on GAM-42 pilot evidence so default hooks match validated API.

sections.heading: Execution Mapping (Linear)
sections.body:
Policy check applied before Linear mutations: GAM-23, GAM-24, GAM-25, GAM-26.

Epic (GameHub Infra):
• GAM-40 — EPIC: Ratings rollout for existing games + hub surfacing

Task breakout with codex assignment + dependencies (blocker -> blocked):
• GAM-41 (dep:ready, dep:critical-path) — Shared widget primitives + UX contract [owner: codex via agent:core/exec:hybrid]
• GAM-41 -> GAM-42 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Representative-game pilot integration (must include at least one legacy/non-shared page)
• GAM-42 -> GAM-43 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Scale retrofit to all active games (`archived !== true`)
• GAM-41 -> GAM-44 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Hub aggregate avg/count surfacing with request-budget guardrail
• GAM-43 -> GAM-45 and GAM-44 -> GAM-45 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — QA harness + security/RLS validation
• GAM-41 -> GAM-46 and GAM-42 -> GAM-46 (dep:blocked) — Generation template contract update after pilot validation

Scheduling semantics:
• In-degree 0 frontier at creation time: GAM-41 only.
• All other tasks are Backlog with dep:blocked labels and explicit blocked-by relations until dependencies clear.

sections.heading: Recommended Next Move
sections.body: Execute GAM-41 first (single in-degree=0 task). After completion, run GAM-42 and GAM-44 as dependency frontier tasks, then GAM-43, then GAM-46 (after GAM-42 evidence), and finally GAM-45 for full rollout closure evidence.

title: Game Skill Improvement Plan
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Quality gates, playtest rubric, skill refactor, and rating system — the full roadmap for making generated games reliably good.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Codex reviewed the game-generator skill and proposed an improvement plan focused on: deterministic hard gates, a soft playtest rubric, skill structure refactoring, and a rating system. The recommended immediate milestone is shipping validate_game.js + soft rubric + a generator → reviewer → repair loop.

sections.heading: 1. Define Gate Policy
sections.body:
This unlocks everything else. Two layers:

• Hard fail checks — binary pass/fail. Game must pass all of these or it does not publish.
• Soft rubric thresholds — subjective quality. Can trigger a repair attempt rather than a hard block.

Do this before writing any code — the policy drives the validator logic.

sections.heading: 2. Implement validate_game.js (Hard Gate)
sections.body:
A deterministic Node.js script that checks:

• Required constants, functions, and Phaser scenes are present
• Score is monotonic (never decreases)
• Game has an overlay, a submit score flow, and a replay button
• Slug matches the entry in games.json
• games.json contract fields are all present and valid

If any check fails → block publish. No exceptions.

sections.heading: 3. Playtest Agent Rubric (Soft Gate)
sections.body:
A separate agent reviews the generated game on 5 categories, each scored 1–5:

• Visuals — does it look good?
• Gameplay — is the core loop fun?
• Clarity — can you tell what to do?
• Stability — does it run without errors?
• Originality — is it doing something interesting?

Fail conditions: any category < 3, OR average < 3.6, OR stability < 4.

A failed rubric auto-generates a targeted repair prompt for the generator. Max 1 repair loop to keep it fast.

sections.heading: 4. Refactor Skill Structure
sections.body:
No behavior changes — just organization. Split the monolithic SKILL.md into:

• SKILL.md → slim orchestrator/router instructions only
• references/ → design philosophy, visual themes, difficulty curve, scoring rules
• scripts/ → validate_game.js and other tooling

Goal: agents can load only the parts they need. Reduces prompt bloat and makes the skill easier to maintain.

sections.heading: 5. Rating UI + Worker Endpoints
sections.body:
Let humans rate games after playing:

• Per-category rating (1–5) + optional comment
• Submit via Cloudflare Worker
• Display aggregate ratings on game cards and the game hub
• Anti-spam / rate limiting on the Worker side

This gives real feedback to complement the agent rubric.

sections.heading: 6. Rating Export Into Repo
sections.body:
Persist ratings so they survive Worker deploys:

• Snapshot JSON committed on a daily schedule
• Dated history files for trend analysis
• Summary markdown for quick human review

Keeps the data version-controlled and auditable.

sections.heading: Priority Update (2026-02-22)
sections.body:
Updated execution order based on current state:

1) Finish and ship the Supabase-backed ratings system across existing games.
2) Collect human ratings on current games to create a real baseline.
3) Iterate the current game-generator skill using this rating signal + observed failures.
4) Re-analyze the broader Game Skill Improvement Plan and then decide/break out the larger skill refactor tracks.

This intentionally delays the larger refactor breakdown until post-ratings evidence exists.

title: Backend Direction: Move from Worker Persistence to Supabase
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Decision: switch to client → Supabase direct for leaderboard/ratings to maximize prototyping speed and simplify growth. No legacy score migration.

sections.heading: What we discussed
sections.body: We wanted the fastest path for a 2-dev team building GameHub with future feedback/ratings and leaderboard ranking support. Main constraints: keep it simple, remove free-tier write bottlenecks, and avoid overengineering.

sections.heading: Tradeoffs
sections.body:
Cloudflare Worker persistence:
• Pros: already deployed
• Cons: free-tier write constraints and weaker long-term fit for richer persistence

Firestore:
• Pros: solid managed platform
• Cons: less natural for SQL-style leaderboard/rating analytics

Supabase:
• Pros: rapid prototyping, straightforward relational model, SQL for rankings/aggregates, easy future auth path
• Cons: requires clean RLS setup

sections.heading: Decision
sections.body:
Choose Supabase now.

Architecture: start with direct client → Supabase access (with RLS), and add a custom API later only if anti-cheat/business logic needs it.

We will not migrate old Worker scores; start fresh.

sections.heading: Concise migration plan
sections.body:
1) Stand up Supabase project and minimal schema for current scope only (games, leaderboard_scores, game_ratings).
2) Replace Worker reads/writes in game templates with Supabase client calls.
3) Enable and verify RLS policies for safe read/write behavior.
4) Cut over and validate end-to-end with fresh data.
5) Defer broader object modeling until after stability.

sections.heading: Next actions
sections.body:
• Create Supabase project + env config
• Implement minimal tables + indexes
• Update game template integration
• Validate leaderboard/rating flows in production
• Remove Worker persistence dependency from templates

title: Linear MCP Integration Plan (v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: MCP-native Linear integration for Discord-driven long-running work using a single-team-first model, label-based routing, and GameHub architecture planning with clear scale-up triggers.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Goal: move operational work tracking to Linear via its hosted MCP server, while keeping strategic planning in GameHub planning pages. Starting assumption: zero setup.

sections.heading: Captured Decisions
sections.body:
• Start with one Linear workspace.
• Start with a single Linear team for now (same two operators + spawned workers).
• Explicit Discord requests can create tasks immediately (no second approval).
• If agent wants to create tasks without explicit request, ask first.
• Routing uses labels + project/epic context (team split deferred).
• Agents should manage most status movement.
• No dedicated intake triage at v1.

sections.heading: Workspace Schema (v1)
sections.body:
Team: GH (single team for v1).

Labels:
• source:discord | source:planning | source:automation
• exec:agent | exec:human | exec:hybrid
• agent:gamegen | agent:core | agent:ops
• lane:gamegen | lane:core | lane:ops
• kind:epic | kind:task | kind:bug | kind:research

Structure:
• Use Projects/Epics for strategic grouping and architecture tracks.
• Use labels for routing/ownership lanes.
• Keep one shared status model across all work.

Issue conventions: owner target, acceptance criteria, priority (P0-P3), automation allowed (yes/no).

sections.heading: Execution Flow
sections.body: Discord mention/request -> intake agent drafts structured issue -> Linear issue created via MCP -> confirmation message returns with link + route summary. Long-running work defaults to issue creation; one-shot chat help does not. Route workers by lane labels within the single team.

sections.heading: MCP/Skill Operating Pattern
sections.body: Use a read-first, write-second workflow: clarify scope/team/priority, list/search/get context, then create/update in logical batches, then summarize blockers and next actions. Preferred endpoint: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (streamable HTTP).

sections.heading: Further Discussion Needed (lil nug + vim)
sections.body:
1) Which issue types/labels (if any) require human signoff before Done?
2) What exact status names should automation use in your workspace?
3) What objective trigger should move us from one team to multiple teams (e.g., backlog size, workflow divergence, reporting needs)?
4) Autonomous task creation boundaries outside explicit asks.

sections.heading: Initial Success Metrics
sections.body: Track intake-to-issue time, cycle time by lane, agent completion %, reopen rate, and architecture epic progress trend.

title: Morning Standup Updates: 6AM Capture + 7AM Messenger (Low-Token, Deterministic)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Replace flaky fan-out orchestration with deterministic two-phase cron design: section capture jobs at 6:00/6:10/6:20 with idempotent success checks, then a 7:00 messenger job that reads artifacts and posts one formatted Discord update.

sections.heading: Disposition (2026-02-24)
sections.body: Status: RETIRED / SUPERSEDED. Superseded by `unified-subagent-orchestration-platform-v1` as the unified orchestration model. Keep for historical reference only; do not execute as active plan unless explicitly re-approved.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Publish one reliable, concise morning update in #morning-standup while minimizing token use and avoiding non-deterministic inter-session handoff behavior.

sections.heading: Design Principles
sections.body:
1) Deterministic over clever: each job has one purpose and clear inputs/outputs.
2) Idempotent capture: if a section already succeeded for the day, skip rework.
3) Low-token by default: retrieve only latest needed data and summarize tersely.
4) Fail-soft posting: messenger always posts at 7:00 with explicit missing-section notes.

sections.heading: Locked Acceptance Gates
sections.body:
1) Artifact schema locked to required fields + enums defined in Artifact Contract.
2) Linear query bounds locked: yesterday completed = Done transitions in previous PT day; stale = >72h since update.
3) Discord read bound locked: N=20 messages max per channel per attempt.
4) Messenger fallback wording locked as defined in Messenger Job (7:00).

sections.heading: Data Sources (fixed)
sections.body:
• Janitor summary source: Discord channel `1475309759300239380` (latest relevant messages only).
• Bug scanner source: Discord channel `1475384413801021542` (latest relevant messages only).
• Work planning source: live Linear state for completed-yesterday + recommended-next + stale/blocked >3d.
• Locked Discord read bound: each capture reads at most latest `N=20` messages from its channel per attempt.

sections.heading: Execution Model
sections.body:
Phase A (Capture): exactly THREE isolated capture agents/jobs (one per section) run on the retry windows at 6:00, 6:10, 6:20 AM PT.
- Agent 1: Janitor capture
- Agent 2: Bug scanner capture
- Agent 3: Linear capture
Each agent owns only its section artifact and never writes others.
Phase B (Publish): one messenger job runs at 7:00 AM PT, reads the three artifacts, and posts one formatted digest to #morning-standup (`1475524028080066640`).
No additional orchestrator layer.

sections.heading: Capture Jobs (6:00 / 6:10 / 6:20)
sections.body:
Use THREE section-specific capture jobs (not one generic job):
• janitor-capture job
• bugscanner-capture job
• linear-capture job
Each job runs at 6:00, 6:10, and 6:20 AM PT and must:
1) Compute PT date key (YYYY-MM-DD).
2) Check its own section artifact first; if already `success`, exit with NO_REPLY.
3) Retrieve only its scoped data source.
4) Write compact JSON artifact with status + payload + attempt metadata.
5) On retrieval/parsing error, write `failed` with reason code and allow next retry window.

sections.heading: Retry Strategy (lazy + deterministic)
sections.body:
• Retry schedule is time-based and deterministic: each of the 3 capture jobs runs at 6:00, 6:10, 6:20.
• Jobs retry only if their own section is not already `success` for the day.
• Hard cap: max 3 attempts per section/day.
• Reason codes (minimal set): `source_read_error`, `parse_error`, `timeout`, `empty_result`.
• Attempt windows are locked per source:
  - Janitor/Bug scanner: latest 20 messages each attempt
  - Linear completed-yesterday: issues transitioned to Done between PT 00:00-23:59 previous day
  - Linear stale: In Progress/Backlog items with no update >72h

sections.heading: Artifact Contract
sections.body:
Artifact dir: `/home/mattc/.openclaw/workspace-codex-gamehub/.openclaw/morning-digest/`
Files (per PT day):
- `YYYY-MM-DD-janitor.json`
- `YYYY-MM-DD-bugscanner.json`
- `YYYY-MM-DD-linear.json`

Locked schema (required fields):
`{ section, dateKey, status, attemptCount, lastAttemptAt, reasonCode, summary, bullets, sourceWindow }`
- `section`: `janitor|bugscanner|linear`
- `dateKey`: PT date `YYYY-MM-DD`
- `status`: `success|failed`
- `attemptCount`: integer 1..3
- `lastAttemptAt`: ISO timestamp
- `reasonCode`: `none|source_read_error|parse_error|timeout|empty_result`
- `summary`: short string (<=160 chars)
- `bullets`: array of short strings (0..5)
- `sourceWindow`: short descriptor of what was read (e.g. `last20messages`, `yesterday_pt`)

Validation rule: messenger treats missing required fields as `failed` with reason `parse_error`.

sections.heading: Messenger Job (7:00)
sections.body:
At 7:00 AM PT:
1) Read the three artifacts for current date key.
2) Build one Discord-ready message with fixed section order.
3) Degraded behavior is locked:
   - Missing file -> `Section unavailable (missing artifact after 3 attempts)`
   - Failed file -> `Section unavailable (<reasonCode> after <attemptCount> attempts)`
   - Invalid schema -> `Section unavailable (parse_error after <attemptCount> attempts)`
4) Post exactly once to channel `1475524028080066640`.
5) No secondary channel posting.

sections.heading: Discord Output Format
sections.body:
**GameHub Morning Update — YYYY-MM-DD**
• **Janitor / Criticals:** <1-line summary>
  - <0-3 bullets>
• **Bug Scanner:** <1-line summary>
  - <0-3 bullets>
• **Yesterday Completed (Linear):** <count + short bullets>
• **Today Focus:**
  1) <priority task>
  2) <priority task>
  3) <priority task>
• **Stale/Blocked (>3d):** <short bullets or `none`>

sections.heading: Token Minimization Tactics
sections.body:
• Read bounded message counts from janitor/bug channels (latest N only).
• Prefer short bullet extraction over narrative generation.
• Avoid cross-session chatter and polling loops.
• Skip successful sections in retry windows.
• Keep messenger formatting logic static with lightweight substitutions.

sections.heading: Reliability and Determinism Notes
sections.body:
• Determinism comes from artifact gating + fixed schedule, not agent memory.
• Publish job is independent from capture execution path and always runs.
• A missing section cannot block the final morning update.

sections.heading: Rollout Plan (safe)
sections.body:
1) Implement artifact schema + write paths.
2) Implement one section end-to-end (janitor) and test retries.
3) Add bug scanner + linear sections.
4) Implement messenger formatting/posting.
5) Run one dry day with manual triggers; then enable scheduled runs.

sections.heading: Task Decomposition Guidance
sections.body:
Suggested future subagent tasks:
A) Artifact library + date-key helper
B) Janitor capture job
C) Bug scanner capture job
D) Linear capture job (yesterday done + today next + stale)
E) Messenger formatter/poster
F) Cron wiring + smoke checklist
